samples.question: What sensors measured oxygen?
samples.reason: The question is about meaning (objectives, fuels, conditions, sensors, how investigations differ) — that goes to retrieval.

entry.text: BASS — Burning and Suppression of Solids (PSI-26): How solid fuels burn in microgravity in a flow duct the first version of this experiment. Fuels: Thin and thick flat samples, acrylic spheres, and candles. Conditions: Microgravity wind tunnel in the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS with airflow up to 40 cm/s. Sensors: Video camera with data overlay and 35-mm still camera. How it differs: The original BASS experiment; BASS-II (PSI-25) is its follow-up with more tests and lower oxygen levels.
entry.source_notes: Objective and sensor text: BASS-II Summary Report NASA/TM-20210011385 (BASS hardware section) and PSI page

entry.text: BASS-II — Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (PSI-25): How solid fuels ignite spread and extinguish in microgravity at low airflow. Fuels: PMMA film rods and slabs; SIBAL cloth; Nomex cloth. Conditions: Oxygen 13.6-22.2% airflow 0 to about 55 cm/s in the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS. Sensors: CSA-CP oxygen sensor for oxygen and CO; Carbon Dioxide Monitor for CO2; video camera with data overlay and 35 mm still camera. How it differs: Small-scale solid burning in a flow duct; the only investigation in this table with a full public test-by-test CSV.
entry.source_notes: Objective and sensor text: BASS-II Summary Report NASA/TM-20210011385 (abstract and sensor sections) and PSI page

entry.text: SAME — Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (PSI-102): How smoke moves and is detected in microgravity. Fuels: Smoke from burning materials. Conditions: Smoke in microgravity with no buoyancy to carry it upward. Sensors: Smoke detectors and aerosol sensors; no oxygen sensor. How it differs: Detection not burning: it is about finding a fire not measuring how it spreads.
entry.source_notes: Objective and sensor text: PSI investigation page summary
